<function=python>
<parameter=code>
res = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':45,'col':6}])
def snap(fr):
    d = {}
    for n in fr.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['pixels']==4:
            b=n['boundary']; r0=min(p[0] for p in b); c0=min(p[1] for p in b)
            d[(r0,c0)]=n['color']
    return d
before = snap(last_transition.before_frame)
after = snap(current_frame)
diff = [(k,before.get(k),after.get(k)) for k in sorted(set(before)|set(after)) if before.get(k)!=after.get(k)]
print(len(diff),"changed")
for k,a,b in diff: print(k,a,'->',b)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

Three possibilities! Ambiguous. Spatially, the most natural is: the cycle goes down the left column, jumps across, and goes up the right column... let me think about the geometry: the chevron is at the bottom of the upper-right cross (25,45). Hmm.
Option A: ...(51,45)→(9,15)→(9,45)→(12,45)→(15,45)→(18,45)→(21,45)→(12,15)→(15,15)... — this jumps (9,15)→(9,45) (across the top), then down the right column to (21,45), then jumps back to (12,15)?? Weird, and it crosses.
